definition.proposition: At matched active FLOPs on E1's stack (14.2M dense params, 200M tokens of code-py-v1), a dropless top-2 MoE FFN with 4 experts x 512 lowers clean80 bpc by about 2.7% vs E1, learned routing beats a frozen random router by about 1.3%, and a dense SwiGLU FFN of the same total params (2048 hidden, 1.47x E1's FLOPs) beats the MoE by a further 1.6% at about the same measured wall time on an RTX 5090.

scope.architecture: E1 hybrid (SWA/GDN/attn), MoE FFN in every block

definition.refutation_criteria: REFUTED if a replication at 200M (6 fresh seeds) puts the Welch 95% CI of E60a - E1 at or above 0, or the CI of E60a - E60b including 0

qual: 6 seeds per arm vs E1's 7, registered, LR from the G3 grid at 20M
reason: E60 stage 1 (registered): E60a - E1 = -2.72%, Welch 95% CI [-3.00%, -2.44%], df 10.3 (M1 PASS, D1 new claim); E60a - E60b = -1.31%, paired CI [-1.54%, -1.07%], df 5 (M3 FAIL: learned routing matters, D2); E60c - E1 = -4.21% [-4.58%, -3.84%] (M2 PASS); E60a - E60c = +1.56% [+1.20%, +1.92%] (M2b PASS). Wall time per 200M run: E60a 5.05 min, E60c 5.19 min.

verified_at.basis: HEAD of the checkout when the event was recorded

limitations.text: LRs chosen on seed 0 at 20M (G3 grid; all three arms picked 6e-3) and not re-checked at 200M; code-py-v1 (not the deduplicated v2); M5 (expert-share balance) not measured because the runs did not save router statistics; E1's 7 reference seeds come from the Phase 2b-5090 campaign, so E60 vs E1 is not paired by seed.

reason: Outside review 2026-11-23 12:10 (over-claim in the v0.5.0 entry's reading), confirmed

limitations.text: E60c vs E60a is parameter-matched, not compute-matched: E60c's dense 2048 FFN costs about 2x the FFN matmuls of E60a's 2-of-4 x 512 active experts (1.47x E1's total FLOPs). The near-equal wall time (5.19 vs 5.05 min) says the MoE gather overhead offsets that difference at this scale; it is not equal compute.
